scope: bit-exact map of the ps block prologue read from 0x471980, and the contradiction it exposes
prologue_map: 0x4719BE  [ecx+0x3BA0] = 0        ; ps count reset to zero on entry
0x471A20  memcpy(0x58 bytes from 0xDA9920) -> a zeroed template at [ebp-0xBC]
0x471A36  cmp [edi],0 ; jne 0x471CAC     ; pre-existing stream error -> exit
0x471A3E  call 0x447190 -> READ BIT 1     ; has-ps: 0 => exit at 0x471CAC, 1 => continue
0x471A4D  call 0x447190 -> READ BIT 2     ; mode: 1 => last = bit+1, 0 => read 5 bits
0x471B9E  call 0x447190 -> READ NEXT BIT  ; per-field present: 1 => skip field, 0 => delta
0x471BE7..0x471C00 counter++ and compare  ; next field via 0x471C11, or loop back via 0x471CA3
the_contradiction: by this map our accepted body sets bit 1308 = 1 (has-ps), bit 1309 = 0 (mode), bits 1310..1314 = 0 (last), bit 1315 = 0 (present)
so the client should proceed to the delta call at 0x471BC8 and the Slot probe at 0x471BB3 should fire at least once
but it never fires and the Decide probe reads loop_c8 = 0 and slot_d0 = 0 with stream_error = 0
so either the ps block is entered at a bit other than 1308 despite the trace, or one of the early branches exits before 0x471B9E
candidate_exit_paths_before_the_present_: 0x4719D0 cmp eax,esi ; jne 0x4719E0 - if the argument [ebp+0x10] is 0, [ebp-0xC0] becomes 0x1869F and the slot path is skipped, but execution still reaches 0x471B9E
0x4719E0 cmp [eax+0x3BA0],esi ; jg 0x4719F4 - if the peer ps count is 0 the same happens
0x471A36 cmp [edi],0 ; jne 0x471CAC - exits only on a pre-existing stream error, which the trace shows as 0
so none of these explains a zero-iteration loop; the next thing to observe is which of 0x471A3E / 0x471A4D / 0x471B9E actually executes
why_this_is_progress: the prologue is now mapped instruction by instruction with the exact bit order (has-ps, mode/last, present, delta)

the remaining uncertainty is a single question - which of the three reads happen - and that is answerable by probing 0x471A3E and 0x471A4D, which are cheaper than 0x471B9E (they run once per snapshot, not once per field)
next: arm 0x471A3E and 0x471A4D (once per snapshot, so much safer than the per-field addresses) and count their hits for the accepted body
if 0x471A3E fires but 0x471A4D does not, the has-ps bit we write is being read as 0 and the ps entry bit is not 1308
